title: A JSON log formatter with redaction
problem: Write JsonFormatter.format so every log record becomes one line of JSON with the time, level, logger name and message, plus any fields passed with extra=, plus the traceback when there is one. Field names that look sensitive are redacted.
requirements: Output is one line of valid JSON per record (newlines in messages or tracebacks stay escaped inside strings)
Keys: time (ISO 8601, UTC, from record.created), level (record.levelname), logger (record.name), message (the message with its %-args applied)
Every field passed with extra= appears as a top-level key; the standard LogRecord attributes (args, msg, lineno, ...) don't
When the record has exception info, add exc with the formatted traceback
Any key containing password, secret, token or authorization (case-insensitive) gets the value "[REDACTED]"
Values json can't encode (dates, sets, objects) are written as str(value)
contract: class JsonFormatter(logging.Formatter): def format(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> str
expectedBehavior: logger.info("order %s placed", 42, extra={"request_id": "r-1"}) writes {"time": "2026-11-12T10:00:00.123456+00:00", "level": "INFO", "logger": "shop", "message": "order 42 placed", "request_id": "r-1"} on one line.
edgeCases: logger.exception(...) inside an except block: traceback included, still one line
extra keys with mixed case like Authorization or api_token
A date or another non-JSON value in extra
Lazy %-style args must be applied (record.msg alone is the unformatted template)
hints: Conceptual: extra= doesn't create a dict on the record; it sets attributes on the LogRecord. So the extra fields are exactly the record's attributes that a plain LogRecord doesn't have.

Specific: get the standard attribute names once by creating an empty LogRecord and looking at vars() of it (plus 'message' and 'asctime', which formatting adds). Use record.getMessage() for the text, self.formatException(record.exc_info) for the traceback, and json.dumps(..., default=str).

Implementation: STANDARD = set(vars(logging.LogRecord("", 0, "", 0, "", None, None))) | {"message", "asctime"}; build a dict with the four fixed keys, add every (key, value) from vars(record) whose key isn't in STANDARD, add exc if record.exc_info, then replace sensitive keys' values, then return json.dumps(entry, default=str).
evaluation: Redaction happens after all fields are collected, so it also covers extra fields
No print(); the formatter only returns the string and the handler writes it
